correctness.rationale: A nontrivial normal subgroup of a finite nilpotent group meets the center, so separation of the prime-order torsion of Z(G) suffices. By Schur's lemma each irreducible summand contributes one character at each prime, forcing at least R summands. Each E_i must be detected by a constituent nonlinear on E_i. The extraspecial degrees are 1 and w_i, with exactly the degree-w_i types nontrivial on the center: for a nontrivial central character the character vanishes off the center by conjugation by an element with a nontrivial central commutator, and character norm then gives degree sqrt(|E_i:Z(E_i)|). Tensor products multiply these costs. For any support S, its cost is at least 1+Σ_{i∈S}(w_i−1) and also at least Σ_{i∈S}w_i, by w_i≥2. Summing both bounds forces Σ_i w_i+max(0,R−t). For equality choose N=max(t,R) rows, one nonlinear E_i on its own row and none on the extra rows. At p_i its row detects Z(E_i), and the remaining N−1 rows can carry an independent set of characters for A[p_i]; at any other prime use up to N rows. These independent prime-wise characters extend to A and can be combined on each row. This covers trivial A, abelian Sylow factors, and all exponents in A.
residual_risks: The frozen checker reports bounded support optimizations and exact small images, not an independent replay or proof for all groups. The proof assumes distinct extraspecial primes and complex representations.

evidence: Theorem 1.3 of Bardestani et al. gives an exact formula for two-step p-groups with cyclic commutator, including a single Sylow factor E_i times an abelian p_i-group, not the mixed-prime product. Kaur et al. (2023) cover two noncyclic distinct-prime factors with cyclic centers. Kaur et al. (2026) Theorem 2 concerns same-prime additivity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The product can use one summand to separate central elements in several Sylow factors with only one multiplicative degree cost; neither summing the Sylow dimensions nor the cyclic-center result computes the arbitrary rank-dependent packing.

evidence: The no-abelian-factor two-extraspecial case agrees with the earlier noncyclic product theorem. The cyclic-factor additivity statements as worded instead predict 3 for D8×C3. A faithful plane representation of D8 has only ±I as scalar images, so twisting by a primitive C3 character gives a faithful dimension-2 representation of the product (and D8 forbids dimension 1).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The contrary additivity statements cannot imply a correct mixed-prime formula. The correct individual and two-factor formulas do not choose the optimal shared rows at arbitrary center ranks.

evidence: Moretó's rdim is the same complex invariant; Lemma 3.4 identifies it with the generator number for abelian groups. Lemma 3.5 uses socle characters for bounds, not this exact optimization.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The socle formulation gives the full-center prime-wise rank constraints, but rank by itself does not determine the degree costs of assembling the nonlinear factors.

value.rationale: The formula computes a standard exact group invariant on a natural family where additivity can fail. It locates precisely when abelian central rank raises the degree above the total compulsory extraspecial cost, and constructs an optimizer. This resolves more than the individual extraspecial degrees, an isolated counterexample, or a small-instance enumeration.
residual_risks: No extension to repeated extraspecial primes or arbitrary nilpotent group factors is asserted.
